objectives.summary: Split a workflow into what Claude does, what people keep and what both share, weighing how reversible, how risky and who answers for it.
Review an intake-to-feedback design for scale, upkeep and access control; find the component likeliest to fail first under stress or misuse.
Choose among workflow, agent, augmented-LLM and Skill-based designs for given reuse, oversight and risk needs, and defend its handoff line.
Review an orchestrator-plus-subagents split against visibility and recovery needs, spotting where boundaries, flow or merging go wrong.
Pick the design that yields the most measurable business value within a cost or SLA cap, comparing proposed features against value goals.
Choose where to deploy (first-party API or a cloud provider) and how to run the agent, trading off residency, hosting, state and custody.

domains.name: Claude Models, Prompting, and Context Engineering

objectives.summary: Choose the model tier meeting every hard limit on speed, spend and quality for a workload, and say why each other tier falls short.
Diagnose why a system prompt gives erratic output; pick the revision that narrows scope and format yet leaves room for acceptable variation.
Match a prompting technique to an observed failure and task difficulty without wasting tokens: examples, reasoning style, structured output.
Study what fills the context and how caching behaves against a budget and call volume to find safe token savings.
Decide where cache breakpoints go and how to package shared material, Skills included, so repeated calls keep hitting the cache.
Set reasoning effort and pick a way to manage context over a long agent run, given latency and accuracy targets.
Audit the tools handed to an agent or its helpers for least privilege; decide which to drop, narrow or swap for a lighter access pattern.
Assess how an integration handles credentials and authorization, find leak and escalation risks, and state the fix for each.
For a system limited chiefly by accuracy or latency, choose the tweak (retrieval depth, tier, caching, call shape) that eases it cheaply.
Trace why a failure in a large agent system went unseen, and choose the monitoring that would have caught it.
Choose between prebuilt RAG, agentic search and whole-corpus context for a corpus and query style; set contextual retrieval and fallbacks.
Compare MCP, direct API or CLI calls, and handing work between agents, on speed, security and state needs, and pick the one that fits.
Weigh revealing context step by step against loading everything first, given the task's context needs and latency tolerance.
Read live error logs and volume figures, then apply the right control (limits, backoff, idempotency, fallback) without double effects.
Review an eval suite after a production miss to find the missing dimension or grading target; define the measure that would have caught it.
Decide what slice of a business workflow makes a sound eval for a given decision, derive success criteria from outcomes, mix test methods.
Diagnose an LLM judge or rubric that disagrees with human reviewers and apply the fix matching the bias at fault.
Design a comparison of two prompt or model setups that stays readable under fixed sample size and spend, with enough repeats to beat noise.
From logs or traces, isolate whether the cause is prompt, retrieval, hallucination, a tool or helper fault, or model mismatch; then fix it.
Read spend and delay telemetry, plus how often the cache is hit, to find where cost concentrates and cut it while holding a quality floor.
Judge readiness to move model versions from deprecation dates and regression results, then pin, retune, re-baseline or wait.
Check where guardrails sit relative to a given abuse route and choose the control that blocks it while keeping valid uses working.
Map where untrusted text (documents, tool output, MCP replies, outside Skills) enters context and set controls so it is never obeyed.
Examine a planned deployment for attack exposure, failure modes, quota exhaustion and supply-chain weakness, and order them by severity.
Place human approval points around steps that are irreversible or carry heavy stakes so runs pause there but low-risk paths keep moving.
Match controls (residency, retention, PII redaction, audit logs, tenant separation) to a compliance duty; pick the set that proves it.
Weigh evidence of unequal outcomes between groups and choose a remedy fitting whether data, prompt framing or eval design is the cause.
Spot a promise in early requirements or a proposed SLA the Claude design cannot keep; resolve it by clarifying needs or changing the design.
Critique a draft decision record that ignores a stakeholder constraint; revise it to state trade-offs and leftover risk without overstating.
Find the hidden assumption, missing dependency or absent runbook step that blocks a new team from operating a Claude system; write the fix.
Plan bundling and company-wide rollout of a team-proven Claude Code workflow, deciding what is centrally enforced and what teams control.
Configure Claude Code or the Agent SDK (modes, hooks, subagents, headless or CI runs) for a team flow inside safety and automation limits.
Examine how a team reviews and owns AI-written code, and name the control that keeps people accountable for it.
